idiom.note: agent_t subclasses on their DIRECT mboxes, messages derived from so_5::message_t, active_obj dispatcher for cores>=2 and one_thread below it

caveats: SWEEP DOCUMENT, NOT A TABLE CELL: the combined_lock waiting time under wait=1 was overridden through QVO_SO_SPIN_WAIT_US=10 microseconds (docs/TUNING.md section 1.2); the adapter's profile is 10 s, SObjectizer's own default 1 ms

cores>=2 uses the active_obj dispatcher (one work thread per agent); cores=1 uses one_thread. The work threads are pinned one per CPU from the harness's set through a custom so_5::disp::abstract_work_thread_factory_t, so SObjectizer gets the same placement qb and CAF get rather than being the one framework left floating
wait=1 maps to combined_lock_factory with a 10 s spin budget (never reached inside a hop); wait=0 maps to simple_lock_factory (mutex + condition variable)

Messages derive from so_5::message_t and travel on each agent's DIRECT mbox. Both of SObjectizer's shipped ping-pong samples use a shared mbox instead, which is simpler and slower; the faster idiom is used here on purpose
